chains_identified.name: CORS Null-Origin → Credentialed API Access → Session Hijack
chains_identified.description: Attacker hosts an HTML page with a sandboxed iframe (sandbox attribute creates null-origin context). The iframe makes credentialed fetch() calls to the backend API. Because the backend reflects Origin: null with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on ALL routes, the iframe receives authenticated API responses including session tokens/JWTs. Victim only needs to visit the attacker page while authenticated — no XSS required.
steps: Host iframe-sandboxed page on attacker domain (e.g., attacker.io/exploit.html) with <iframe sandbox='allow-scripts' srcdoc='...'> containing credentialed fetch to /auth/me
Victim (authenticated revops.copointdata.com user) visits attacker.io/exploit.html — social engineering via email/LinkedIn
Sandboxed iframe origin resolves to null — backend reflects ACAO: null + ACAC: true
Attacker reads /auth/me response containing user identity, role, session JWT or auth token
Optionally: read /api/auth/csrf for CSRF token, then replay credentialed POST to state-mutating endpoints
Authenticate as victim using extracted session material — account takeover complete
missing_evidence: Victim must visit attacker-controlled page while authenticated — delivery mechanism needed (spear-phish, LinkedIn, compromised ad)
/auth/me response format confirmation — does it return JWT, session cookie value, or user data only
Exact /api/auth/csrf response format to confirm CSRF token extraction path
Confirmation that session cookie is not SameSite=Strict (which would block credentialed cross-origin requests)
chains_identified.cors_null_exploit_vector: sandboxed iframe with srcdoc — null origin created by sandbox attribute, no XSS needed
blocking_issues: victim delivery mechanism — OSINT needed for real user targeting
chains_identified.ev_change_from_wave_1: +0.00 (confirmed critical, EV ceiling at 0.97 pending /auth/me format)

chains_identified.name: OIDC Nonce Bypass → Azure AD Token Replay → Account Takeover
chains_identified.description: NextAuth does not validate the nonce claim in Azure AD OIDC id_tokens. An attacker who can replay a previously captured id_token (or modify claims with a known NEXTAUTH_SECRET) can create a session as any user whose email is known. Azure AD Tenant ID 9046c3d1-04fe-4afe-9e4f-9217f27b5a66 is confirmed.
steps: Obtain a valid Azure AD id_token (from OSINT, phishing, or GitHub leaked client_secret)
Replay the id_token to NextAuth /api/auth/callback/azure-ad endpoint with modified sub/email claims
If NEXTAUTH_SECRET is known (from GitHub leaks), forge the JWT session token directly
Bypass nonce validation — NextAuth session created as victim user
Access authenticated API endpoints as victim
missing_evidence: Active OIDC nonce validation test — must exercise live Azure AD flow to confirm absence
NEXTAUTH_SECRET value (GitHub leaks scan may provide this)
Exact NextAuth version — CVE-2023-48309 applicability depends on version < 4.24.5
blocking_issues: NEXTAUTH_SECRET needed OR active nonce bypass confirmation

chains_identified.name: RBAC IDOR → Role Self-Escalation → Privilege Escalation
chains_identified.description: PUT /rbac/users/{id}/role lacks server-side authorization preventing a user from modifying their own role. An authenticated low-privilege user can enumerate role IDs via /rbac/roles and submit a PUT request assigning themselves admin role.
steps: Authenticate as low-privilege user (via CORS chain or leaked creds)
GET /rbac/roles to enumerate available role IDs including admin
PUT /rbac/users/{own_user_id}/role with admin role ID payload
Confirm role escalation — access admin-only endpoints
missing_evidence: Authenticated session required first (obtain via chain_002 or chain_003)
blocking_issues: requires authenticated session first — dependent on chain_002 or chain_003 success

chains_identified.name: CORS Auth Access → SSRF Endpoints → Azure IMDS Managed Identity Token
chains_identified.description: After obtaining an authenticated session via chain_002, use SSRF-capable endpoints (/proxy, /pdf, /screenshot, /fetch, /render) to probe Azure IMDS at 169.254.169.254. Azure Container Apps with managed identity enabled would return OAuth tokens granting access to Azure resources.
steps: Obtain authenticated session via chain_002 (CORS null-origin exploit)
Probe /proxy?url=http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01 with Metadata:true header
If IMDS accessible: request identity token from /metadata/identity/oauth2/token?resource=https://management.azure.com
Use managed identity token to enumerate Azure resources (Storage, Key Vault, SQL)
Lateral movement to other Azure services or data exfiltration
missing_evidence: SSRF internal routing confirmation — does /proxy forward to internal IPs
Azure managed identity assignment confirmation for the Container App
blocking_issues: chain_002 must succeed first; SSRF internal routing unconfirmed
